newsitem.title: UK: Lloyds on acquisition trail, shares soar.
newsitem.headline: Lloyds on acquisition trail, shares soar.

text.p: Banking group Lloyds TSB Plc told analysts at a results briefing on Friday the company was looking for suitable acquisitions, but if none were identified then a share buy-back was possible.
Shares in the group soared nine percent or 63-1/2p to 739p by 1030 GMT.
"Their preference was for another acquisition," said David Poutney, analyst at Panmure Gordon. "But if none were identified a share buy back was certainly mentioned.
"I expect to see a large acquisition within the next six months and this excites everybody because it would employ surplus capital in a meaningful way."

Another analyst, who declined to be named, described the meeting as very positive. "It was an upbeat meeting, with talk of share buy-backs or dividend increases if they couldn't find an equivalent use for their capital in terms of acquisitions," he said.

The company had also given positive feedback on the retail side of its operations and on the outlook for its TSB branches. But most analysts were dwelling on the possibility of a major acquisition, hoping that Lloyds could generate the sort of cost savings achieved from its merger with TSB.

Earlier, the group reported pre-tax profits of 1.504 billion stg, at the top end of market forecasts, plus a higher-than-expected interim dividend. The shares had initially gained four percent on the favourable results.
